subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class `models status --probe --all` mode for every configured model, or fold this health-check need into fallback-chain or staged migration diagnostics instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent CLI contract makes real provider calls and overlaps other open model-validation workflows, so automation should not choose the product surface alone.

options.title: Approve `--probe --all`
options.body: Add an opt-in all-configured-model probe that reuses the existing status/probe pipeline, keeps default `--probe` unchanged, and documents provider filtering, JSON output, costs, and redaction.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Testing
options.body: Make the fallback-chain validation issue own configured fallback health and keep status probes focused on auth/profile reachability.

options.title: Defer To Migration UX
options.body: Treat model health checks as one step in a staged model migration workflow and avoid adding a standalone status flag for now.

recommendation.title: Approve `--probe --all`
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in all-configured-model probe that reuses the existing status/probe pipeline, keeps default `--probe` unchanged, and documents provider filtering, JSON output, costs, and redaction.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the existing auth-probe behavior and has the clearest history across model status, fallback, and health-check scoping.
